Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "could you turn this into a clear brief for a one-week inventory reconciliation and staff handoff for Cedar Basket Cooperative? the count is for monday, March 18, and the handoff covers March 18 through March 24. Cedar Basket has 34 members and one neighborhood shop, a shared prep room and a delivery porch. volunteers do the counts; there is no barcode scanner, so they use paper count sheets and an inventory workbook. sunday close is the starting point, and the next supplier delivery is due wednesday morning. we need a usable request for a checklist, a count worksheet and a short handoff memo, not a general inventory policy.

this is the first count after the winter pantry drive. the workbook was last updated sunday at closing, but two volunteers entered donated stock on separate paper slips and neither slip has been copied into the workbook. those slips are in the blue folder by the office desk. one says six jars of apricot jam, and the other says twelve bags of rice. both donations are on the delivery porch, not in the shop yet. ask the person making the count to check both slips and physically verify those items before combining them with the on-hand total. don't assume that a paper entry means the food has been put away. the prep room has a whiteboard for temporary notes, but its figures are not the official record.

for the counted items, use these sunday workbook quantities and monday physical counts: tinned tomatoes, 42 cans in the workbook and 35 found, lot T24-031, best-before November 30, 2026; red lentils, 18 bags and 16 found; flour, 100 bags and 99 found; eggs, 30 trays and 30 found. the tomato cans are intact, and the missing seven were not located in the shop, prep room, porch or member pickup area during the first count. we have not established whether they were sold, moved or entered incorrectly. there are no lot details supplied for the lentils, flour or eggs, so don't make any up. the flour is stored in the dry-stock aisle and the eggs are in the walk-in cooler. the jam and rice slips are separate from these four workbook lines.

the reconciliation rule needs to be explicit for every SKU, and it should not quietly turn a discrepancy into a confirmed loss. if the absolute difference between the workbook quantity and the physical count is greater than four units or greater than three percent of the workbook quantity, whichever limit is crossed first, mark that line unresolved, keep only the affected stock out of new allocations, and request a recount by a second volunteer before changing the workbook. if the difference is no more than four units and no more than three percent, enter the physical count in the workbook after the counter initials the paper sheet. state the alternative branch too. don't hold an entire food category because one line is unresolved, and don't treat the workbook as proof of what is physically present. the discrepancy decision should be recorded next to the count, not hidden in a separate total.

there's a cooler note to include carefully. the sunday log for the walk-in reads 4.8°C at 6:00 p.m., 5.6°C at 6:30 p.m. and 4.9°C at 7:00 p.m.; readings are normally written every half hour. the note does not establish how long the temperature stayed above 5°C. the coordinator has arranged a technician check for tuesday at 8:00 a.m., but that result is not available yet. include this instruction in the handoff: if the technician's tuesday reading is above 5°C, keep dairy lot D-18 on hold and notify the coordinator; if it is 5°C or below, do not extend the hold on the basis of that tuesday reading alone, and record the reading. the hold applies to D-18, not all chilled food. don't state that the cooler is safe or unsafe based on the sunday entries, and don't write an outcome for the pending check.

please build the brief around the following numbered work sequence, while making it easy to use at the shop:
1. gather the blue-folder slips, the sunday workbook and blank paper sheets; identify the counter and the second volunteer who can do recounts.
2. count the listed stock in its named storage areas, check the two donation slips against the physical jam and rice, and write the observed quantities and initials on paper.
3. apply the threshold rule separately to each workbook line; note any unresolved line and the limited hold, or enter a permitted correction after initials.
4. copy verified changes and unresolved notes into the inventory workbook, leaving a visible record of the earlier sunday quantity rather than replacing it without a trail.
5. pass the cooler instruction and the pending tuesday check to the next shift, then include any known next step without pretending the technician has already reported.

the wednesday supplier delivery includes 24 cartons of oat milk, two crates of carrots and one box of paper labels. the delivery is expected, not yet received; the receiving volunteer should count it against the delivery note when it arrives and add the received quantity only after checking it. no supplier price or delivery shortage has been reported. include the arrival in the week handoff so it is not mistaken for stock already counted on monday. a member pickup is booked for tuesday afternoon for three flour bags and one jam jar, but the pickup has not happened yet. show it as a scheduled movement, not as a monday deduction; the jam jar must come from the donated porch stock if that stock is verified. if the porch stock is not verified, leave the jam source unresolved for the pickup rather than taking a jar from an unconfirmed total.

keep the requested deliverable practical for volunteer use: a dated checklist, a compact worksheet with columns for item, storage area or source, sunday workbook quantity where supplied, monday count, difference, lot or date detail where supplied, initials and next action; then a short handoff memo for the March 18–24 shifts. include the numbered work sequence above and the exact cooler decision branches. quote the coordinator's note in the memo as, “Please leave the dairy hold tied to lot D-18 until the Tuesday check is written down.” don't turn that quotation into a broader instruction about every refrigerated product. if information is not supplied, mark it as not supplied rather than filling it in. end with the handoff details for the later shifts, including the pending tuesday reading, the not-yet-received wednesday delivery and the scheduled tuesday pickup; don't add a result, approval or recommendation.", "output": "Please prepare a practical one-week inventory reconciliation and staff handoff for Cedar Basket Cooperative. The count is for Monday, March 18, and the handoff covers March 18 through March 24. Cedar Basket has 34 members, one neighborhood shop, a shared prep room and a delivery porch. Volunteers use paper count sheets and an inventory workbook because there is no barcode scanner. Use Sunday closing as the starting point; the next supplier delivery is expected Wednesday morning. Create a dated checklist, a compact count worksheet and a short handoff memo, rather than a general inventory policy.

### Inventory records and donated stock

This is the first count after the winter pantry drive. The workbook was last updated at Sunday closing. Two volunteers recorded donated stock on separate paper slips, but neither slip has been copied into the workbook. The slips are in the blue folder by the office desk: one lists six jars of apricot jam, and the other lists twelve bags of rice. Both donations are on the delivery porch, not in the shop. Ask the counter to check the slips and physically verify the jam and rice before including them in an on-hand total. A paper entry does not establish that the food has been put away. The prep-room whiteboard is for temporary notes, not the official record.

Use these Sunday workbook quantities and Monday physical counts:

| Item | Sunday workbook quantity | Monday count | Details |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Tinned tomatoes | 42 cans | 35 cans | Lot T24-031; best-before November 30, 2026 |
| Red lentils | 18 bags | 16 bags | No lot details supplied |
| Flour | 100 bags | 99 bags | Dry-stock aisle; no lot details supplied |
| Eggs | 30 trays | 30 trays | Walk-in cooler; no lot details supplied |

The tomato cans are intact. The missing seven cans were not found in the shop, prep room, porch or member pickup area during the first count. It is not established whether they were sold, moved or entered incorrectly. Do not assign lot details to the lentils, flour or eggs. The donated jam and rice slips are separate from these four workbook lines.

### Reconciliation rule

Apply the rule separately to every SKU, and do not present a discrepancy as a confirmed loss. If the absolute difference between the workbook quantity and the physical count is greater than four units or greater than three percent of the workbook quantity, whichever limit is crossed first, mark the line unresolved, keep only the affected stock out of new allocations, and request a recount by a second volunteer before changing the workbook. If the difference is no more than four units and no more than three percent, enter the physical count in the workbook after the counter initials the paper sheet. State both branches clearly. Do not hold an entire food category because one line is unresolved, and do not treat the workbook as proof of what is physically present. Record the discrepancy decision beside the count, not only in a separate total.

### Cooler handoff

The Sunday walk-in log reads 4.8°C at 6:00 p.m., 5.6°C at 6:30 p.m. and 4.9°C at 7:00 p.m. Readings are normally written every half hour. The log does not establish how long the temperature stayed above 5°C. A technician check is arranged for Tuesday at 8:00 a.m.; its result is not yet available. Include these exact decision branches in the handoff: if the technician’s Tuesday reading is above 5°C, keep dairy lot D-18 on hold and notify the coordinator; if it is 5°C or below, do not extend the hold on the basis of that Tuesday reading alone, and record the reading. The hold applies to D-18, not to all chilled food. Do not declare the cooler safe or unsafe based on the Sunday entries, or state an outcome for the pending check.

### Numbered work sequence

1. Gather the blue-folder slips, Sunday workbook and blank paper sheets. Identify the counter and the second volunteer who can perform recounts.
2. Count the listed stock in its named storage areas. Check the donation slips against the physical jam and rice, and write observed quantities and initials on paper.
3. Apply the threshold rule separately to each workbook line. Note an unresolved line and its limited hold, or enter a permitted correction after initials.
4. Copy verified changes and unresolved notes into the inventory workbook. Leave a visible record of the earlier Sunday quantity rather than replacing it without a trail.
5. Pass the cooler instruction and pending Tuesday check to the next shift. Include any known next step without implying that the technician has reported.

### Upcoming movements

The Wednesday supplier delivery is expected to include 24 cartons of oat milk, two crates of carrots and one box of paper labels. It has not yet been received. Ask the receiving volunteer to count it against the delivery note when it arrives and add received quantities only after checking them. No supplier price or delivery shortage has been reported. Include the expected arrival in the week handoff so it is not mistaken for stock counted Monday.

A member pickup is scheduled for Tuesday afternoon for three flour bags and one jam jar; it has not happened yet. Show it as a scheduled movement, not as a Monday deduction. The jam jar must come from the donated porch stock if that stock is verified. If the porch stock is not verified, leave the jam source unresolved for the pickup rather than taking a jar from an unconfirmed total.

The worksheet should have columns for item, storage area or source, Sunday workbook quantity where supplied, Monday count, difference, lot or date detail where supplied, initials and next action. Include the numbered work sequence and the exact cooler decision branches. In the memo, quote the coordinator’s note exactly: “Please leave the dairy hold tied to lot D-18 until the Tuesday check is written down.” Do not broaden that quotation into an instruction about every refrigerated product. Mark information that was not supplied as not supplied. End the handoff with the later-shift details: the pending Tuesday reading, the Wednesday delivery that has not yet been received, and the scheduled Tuesday pickup. Do not add a result, approval or recommendation."}]
